title: A Framework for Identifying, Categorizing, and Explaining Bias in AI-Generated Code

bias_targets.methodology: Manual annotation of AI-generated Python code snippets and evaluation of LLMs using In-Context Learning (ICL) to detect positive or negative semantic associations between attributes and descriptors in variable names, identifiers, and comments.
Manual labeling and automated LLM-based classification of code snippets to identify logic that encodes generalized beliefs or associates positive/negative traits with demographic groups.

Evaluating AI-generated Python code using manual annotations and LLM zero-shot/few-shot prompts to detect differential behavior, advantages, or restrictions based explicitly on protected attributes like gender, race, or age.
Detection of the omission, misrepresentation, or exclusionary coding of certain identities in data structures and enumerations, assessed via a multi-label taxonomy and LLM classification.

Identifying the use of rigid, arbitrary numeric boundaries tied to protected or non-protected attributes to determine eligibility or disparate outcomes, measured through expert consensus coding and LLM-based bias justification.

Evaluating whether non-sensitive variables (e.g., occupation) are used in code logic as stand-ins for protected attributes, causing indirect discrimination, assessed via manual auditing and LLM in-context learning prompts.
